text:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] SEV-1: GPU pool 'eu-central-2-gpu-pool-1' reporting 100% allocation + failed scale attempts for 9m. Inference-router queue growing fast. Paging @Sam (oncall)

Sam (oncall): on it. seeing sustained queue growth -> ~3.1k pending, 500-level throttles for some customers. Headline: autoscaler attempts rejected with placement_errors.

Ravi: digging into infer-autoscaler: lots of "allocation_rejected: incompatible_mig_sizes" in the last 12m. Looks different -- we have mixed MIG profiles after last week's rolling upgrade: 1g.1slice + 1g.2slice present.

Chen: interesting — infra metrics show 27 nodes with tiny leftover slices (0.5-1 slice) that can't satisfy requests that require 2-slice MIG. Free GPU capacity exists but is unusable.

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended mitigations: 1) enable emergency_degrade for non-enterprise routes, 2) create emergency uniform-nodegroup, 3) trigger consolidation drains. See /runbooks/gpu-fragmentation.

Sam (oncall): start mitigation plan: A) turn on emergency degrade -> route lower-priority traffic to CPU fallback embeddings; B) create emergency nodegroup with uniform 2-slice MIGs and increase pool cap; C) perform conservative drains to consolidate fragments. Priya (who's on CS?) can we get customer triage?

Customer Success (Tess): two paying customers in EU experiencing timeouts on batched embeddings. One has a big nightly job running now. Their SRE is live. They want ETA.

Maya: toggle emergency_degrade for pay-as-you-go tag now. Patch:
```json
{"emergency_degrade": {"enabled": true, "target": "cpu-embed-fallback", "affected_tags": ["payg"]}}
```

incidents-bot: deployment event -> configpatch/emergency-degrade v1.2 started.

Ravi: autoscaler failure sample log: 
```
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z ERROR allocation_rejected request_id=abc123 reason=incompatible_mig_sizes required=2s available_slices=[1s,1s,1s,1s]
```
We need homogeneous capacity for these allocation profiles.

Chen: I can spin a uniform nodegroup of 2-slice MIG nodes in eu-central-2. Creating nodepool-urgent-2slice. Will take ~7-9m for provisioning. Increasing pool cap to 150 -> request submitted.

Sam (oncall): submitted quota bump for pool max to 150. Infra, please confirm.

infra-bot: Quota update request accepted. Pool max_replicas increased to 150 pending node creation.

Ravi: while nodes come up, run consolidation script to squeeze fragments into fewer nodes. Using conservative 2-at-a-time drain to avoid cold-KV storms. Script:
```bash
# find underpacked nodes
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-frag=true -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c "kubectl drain {} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=3m && sleep 40"
```

Maya: note — draining will evict live inference pods and might temporarily increase tail latency. Let's exclude enterprise-tagged pods from eviction; we only want to consolidate best-effort capacity.

Sam (oncall): set label selector to exclude enterprise: true in drain script. Also toggle conservative_binpack=false to relax binpacking constraints for 15m.

Ravi: permissive binpack flag set for 15m. Also triggered throttling rule: non-critical batch jobs reduced to 10% concurrency to shrink pressure.

(8m later)

infra-bot: nodepool-urgent-2slice provisioning complete: +28 nodes added. Autoscaler now has headroom. Pending allocations starting to succeed.

Ravi: consolidation run reduced fragmented slices from 27 -> 6. Allocation rejection rate dropped from 78% -> 6%. Queue length dropped from 3100 -> 420.

eng-ml: note — emergency_degrade caused CPU fallback for many payg customers. Latency increased for those requests but they succeed. We'll need to run evals post-incident for quality drift.

Customer Success (Tess): customers report improvement. One customer still sees occasional 5xxs; their batch job is massive. We're coordinating a warm window with them.

Chen: monitoring for KV cache warming and cold-start latency. Observing additional cross-node KV fetches due to permissive binpack. Tail latency for some models spiked ~120ms for cold requests.

Sam (oncall): current metrics: queued 420, 429s ~0.9%, 5xxs trending down. Good. Keeping permissive_binpack for another 10m then revert. Keep emergency nodepool until day after for capacity cushion.

Ravi: action items for post-incident: 1) add fragmentation-aware allocator to infer-autoscaler, 2) nightly consolidation job to avoid accumulation of small fragments, 3) add warning when mixed-MIG profiles present in a pool, 4) require canary for MIG profile changes.

Maya: ops follow-ups: notify customers formally, compute cost impact of emergency nodes and quota bump, schedule remediation sprint. eng-ml will own fallback quality evals.

Sam (oncall): prepping postmortem doc now. Root cause summary: mixed MIG profiles after rollout + strict binpack policy + sudden large batched embedding workloads -> stranded GPU fragments and autoscaler rejections. Mitigations applied: emergency degrade, new uniform nodepool, conservative drains, permissive binpack, temporary throttles.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident severity lowered to SEV-2. Suggested writeup template: /templates/postmortem-minor.

(Hand-off)

Sam (oncall): handing off to Maya for follow-ups. Key status: pool headroom added, queue reduced, permissive binpack scheduled to revert. Creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners.

Maya: taking over. I'll post the initial postmortem link here once created and open remediation tickets. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Thread archived after oncall handoff.
